contexts.text: The greatest delight (of the antediluvians) consists in one holding another subject to himself.
Were they to be subject as to the things of the understanding and will. Signified, Explained.
That the truths of the Natural were adjoined and subjected to the Internal. Signified, Explained. AC 5649.
The renunciation and subjection of all things which are of service to the Church. Signified, Explained.
That all things were subject to the Natural which is under the auspices of the Internal. Signified, Explained. AC 6162.
To be subject, and to serve (as Issachar does). Signified.
They would subject the things of Heaven in themselves to those of Hell.
The apparent love and friendship between consorts, one of whom is subjugated, and thence subject to the other. Explained.

Still (these opposites) are held in connection by a wonderful subjection of all Hell under Heaven, of evil under good, and of falsity under truth; of which subjection we have treated in the work on Heaven and Hell.
They had previously loved nothing more than to excogitate methods by which they could subject others to themselves. (Such there become sorcerers.)
